feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is stated for it. Evidence: in iteration 1, the +/-0.03 m span with 12 mm footprints and 0.06 m lead gave the best result so far (score 631.8; s-bend 16/20, oval 20/20 at 1.84 s), but the slalom stayed at 0/20 with 1.05 line-loss events and max_error 0.064. In iteration 2, the 16 mm footprint gave no slalom gain (0/20, 1.0 line-loss events, max_error 0.0646) and cut s-bend finishes to 15/20. In iteration 3, lead 0.04 m dropped the oval to 14/20 and the s-bend to 6/20, while the slalom stayed at 0/20. Footprint and lead have therefore been ruled out as the slalom fix, which points to turn authority. Next-race decisions: if slalom line_loss_events fall below about 1.0 but no trial finishes, keep wheel_track at 0.10 m and make no other change. If the oval loses trials at 0.10 m (off-track), return to 0.11 m. If s-bend or slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, narrow the span to +/-0.025 m with 0.0083 m pitch rather than reducing wheel_track further.
requested_changes: Keep wheel_track at 0.10 m. Iteration 1 showed slalom line loss (1.05 events) is the failure, and a narrower track adds turn authority at the direction changes. If slalom line-loss events fall but no trial finishes, report the max_error at exit and do not change the track again.

If the oval finishes fewer than 20/20 trials at 0.10 m (off-track), try wheel_track 0.11 m. Iteration 1 showed the oval at 1.84 s on 0.12 m with 20/20 finishes, so the time margin is there, but the reach at tight turns may not be.

If s-bend or slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 (iteration 1 measured 0.34 on the s-bend), narrow the sensor span to x = +/-0.025 m with 0.0083 m pitch, keeping 12 mm footprints, to reduce jitter from the higher effective gain.
